modern: From Plato: But I would give this man a sufficient answer, which is this: You do not speak well, if you think that a man who is good for anything at all ought to calculate the risk of life or death, and should not rather look only to this in all that he does: whether he is doing what is just or unjust, and the works of a good or a bad man.
original: From Plato: But I would make this man a sufficient answer, which is this: Thou sayest not well, if thou thinkest that a man who is good for anything at all ought to compute the hazard of life or death, and should not rather look to this only in all that he does, whether he is doing what is just or unjust, and the works of a good or bad man.
